terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to price today's first order.

tasks.title: Price the candles
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/prices.js`, make a `const` called `subtotalCents`: the price of one candle (`candlePriceCents`) times the number of candles (`quantity`). Print it.

Check runs your file with other orders in place of the numbers at the top, so build on the names, not on the numbers.
nextSteps: Read the order near the top of the file.
On the right of `=`, combine the two names with the right operator.
hints: Three candles at the same price cost that price three times over.
JavaScript writes "times" as `*`. Both values you need already have names at the top of the file.
The line has the shape `const subtotalCents = ... * ...`, with the price and the quantity names in place of the dots.

tasks.title: Take off the discount
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, make a `const` called `discountCents`: `discountPercent` percent of `subtotalCents`, rounded to the nearest whole cent. Exactly half a cent rounds up. Print it.

Check tries orders where the discount comes out even and orders where it has to be rounded.
nextSteps: Make sure Task 1 passes: the discount is a part of the subtotal.
Work out the percentage: a percent is that many hundredths.
Round the result to a whole number of cents.
Print it and run the file.
hints: Read the part of the lesson on percentages, then think about an order where the result is not a whole number of cents.
`Math` has three ways to make a whole number: one always goes down, one always goes up, and one goes to the nearest.
Wrap the whole percentage sum in `Math.round(...)`: `subtotalCents * discountPercent / 100` inside the brackets.

tasks.title: Find the total
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make a `const` called `totalCents`: the subtotal, minus the discount, plus shipping (`shippingCents`). Print it.

Check runs your file with other orders, including one with free shipping and one with no discount.
nextSteps: Make sure Tasks 1 and 2 pass first.
Under `// Task 3`, make `totalCents` from the three names.
Check each sign: what comes off, and what goes on.
Print it and compare it with the till by hand.
hints: The customer pays for the candles, gets the discount back, and pays for the parcel to travel.
Two of the three values come from your own variables, and one from the order at the top.
Start from `subtotalCents`, take away `discountCents`, then add `shippingCents`.

tasks.title: Count the boxes
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, make a `const` called `boxes`: how many boxes Ines needs for the order, when one box holds `candlesPerBox` candles. A box that is only partly full still counts as a whole box. Print it.

Check tries orders that fill the boxes exactly, orders with candles left over, and other box sizes.
nextSteps: Divide the candles by the box size and look at the result.
Ask what to do when it is not a whole number.
Pick the `Math` helper that makes that choice.
Print it and try it for 8 and for 9 candles in your head.
hints: Nine candles in boxes of four make two full boxes and one candle left over. That candle still needs a box.
Dividing gives 2.25 for nine candles. You want the next whole number, never a smaller one.
`Math.ceil(...)` around `quantity / candlesPerBox` always goes up to the next whole number.
